target_customer: Design minded renters and young urban consumers who want reconfigurable furniture
problem: Cheap flat pack furniture is disposable and fixed in shape, while designer furniture is expensive; people who move often want pieces they can rebuild into new forms.
business_model: Direct to consumer hardware sales of modular aluminum parts and kits, later a Kickstarter relaunch

founders.name: Sejun Park
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he was a manufacturing engineer for Toyota/Lexus; YC bio reads 'I do hardware things'.

exit.reason: Cause not public; YC lists Aalo as Inactive, the .co domain no longer resolves, and no closure announcement was found.

competitors.name: IKEA
competitors.what: Low price flat pack furniture, the main price comparison for Aalo

technical_complexity.rationale: Roughly ten interlocking powder coated aluminum parts joined with an Allen wrench; a small team could design and source it, though manufacturing quality and logistics were real work.

defensibility.rationale: Modular aluminum parts are easy to copy and the company had no reported patents or network effects.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Aalo.

market_need_then: Press framed demand as a reaction to disposable fast furniture; Product Hunt launch on 2018-02-16 drew 234 votes, and TechCrunch covered it in March 2018.

branding.domain_note: Used aalo.co, a .co domain rather than .com; the domain no longer resolves (checked 2026-11).

identity.visual_style: White or black powder coated aluminum parts, minimal industrial look
identity.voice_and_tone: Maker and design geek tone, 'Lego-like furniture', pushes anti disposable furniture

branding.brand_signature: The Lego-like framing of furniture as snap together parts

rebrands.why: Second generation product relaunched on Product Hunt (2019-05-08) and Kickstarter, easier to assemble with stronger recyclable materials; not a name change

branding.community_and_virality: Design press coverage (TechCrunch, Design Milk, Gessato, Yanko Design, InsideHook) and Product Hunt launches in 2018 and 2019; InsideHook mentions a planned online community for sharing designs.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong design press and two Product Hunt launches for a one person company, but no evidence of lasting customer community or sales scale.

outcome_analysis: Aalo was a one person hardware company that earned good design press and two Product Hunt launches, then relaunched as Aalo 2.0 on Kickstarter in 2019. The cause of its becoming inactive is not public, so failure factors are left empty. Funding appears limited to a roughly 120 thousand dollar YC era amount, which is thin for physical product manufacturing.
notes: The 120K figure is reported by two databases (Seedtable lists it as August 2018, CB Insights gives the same total with Y Combinator as investor); no primary source. It is likely the YC deal, so stage is other. Kickstarter 2019 raise amount not found. The only dated competitor is IKEA as a price comparison in the TechCrunch article; no direct modular furniture rival was named. The company website did not resolve in this session.
